children: NHAI extends debarment of PNC Infratech’s concessionaire Awadh Expressway to parent company following damage to a stretch of the Kanpur-Lucknow Expressway

PNC Infratech has been barred from participating in bids floated by the National Highways Authority of India, the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways and their executing agencies for three years following damage to a section of the Kanpur-Lucknow Expressway.

The action comes after NHAI extended the debarment of PNC Infratech’s subsidiary and concessionaire, Awadh Expressway Private Ltd, to the parent company in its capacity as promoter. PNC Infratech said it received the communication from NHAI on 11 September and that both the company and Awadh Expressway are evaluating legal remedies.
Damage To Expressway Stretch Triggers Action

The matter relates to damage to an isolated stretch of the six-lane Kanpur-Lucknow Expressway. PNC Infratech had earlier said heavy and continuous rainfall had affected around 300 metres of the expressway, representing less than 0.5 per cent of its total length.

The affected project, Kanpur-Lucknow Expressway Package-2, has a bid project cost of Rs 1,513 crore. It had received both provisional and final completion certificates and was in the maintenance phase when the damage occurred. PNC had said most of the affected stretches had subsequently been repaired, with work continuing on the remaining portions.
NHAI Had Earlier Issued Show-Cause Notices

The latest debarment follows show-cause notices issued by NHAI to Awadh Expressway over the damage. The earlier proceedings included a proposed penalty equivalent to 2 per cent of the performance security, debarment proceedings against certain technical personnel for up to three years and a proposed downgrade of the concessionaire's Pavement Condition Index rating.
PNC Infratech had previously maintained that it had not been debarred or declared a non-performer by NHAI at that stage and said it was responding to the notices.

The company had also said repair costs were covered under its routine maintenance obligations and that there was no material impact on its financial position, ongoing projects or eligibility to bid for new projects at the time.
Three-Year Restriction Hits New Road Bids

With the latest NHAI communication, the restriction now directly extends to PNC Infratech, preventing it from participating in bids floated by NHAI, MoRTH and their executing agencies for three years.

The company said the order would not affect its status as a going concern or the execution, operation and maintenance of its ongoing projects. It added that it would disclose any financial implications once greater clarity emerges.
The development has also weighed on investor sentiment, with PNC Infratech shares falling sharply in Tuesday's trading session following the NHAI action.
